pages.text: Sia is a shark in the ocean. Sharks are fish, and they breathe using gills on the sides of their body.
Sia’s skeleton is not hard bone like ours. Sharks have cartilage, which is lighter and bendier than bone.
Sia has many teeth. When a tooth falls out, a new tooth can grow and move forward to replace it.
Sia swims forward smoothly. Moving helps water flow past her gills, so she can breathe underwater.
Sia uses strong senses to find food. She can notice movement and smell in the water very well.
Not all sharks are the same size. Some sharks are small, and some are big, but all are ocean fish.
Sia swims calmly and gives space to others. Ocean animals share the water and follow safe distances.
Sia remembers: gills help her breathe, cartilage keeps her light, and teeth can be replaced again and again.
As sunset comes, Sia glides quietly. The ocean is her home, and she moves through it like a smooth shadow.
Bedtime fact: sharks are fish that breathe with gills, and their teeth can replace themselves many times.
